notes:
EU enterprise account (banking). Strong sensitivity to data residency and vendor risk.

Current motion / why now:
- They saw early chatter about our “latency per dollar” benchmark and want to use the report in their internal evaluation packet (architecture review + procurement).
- They’re not looking for “best model” marketing; they want methodology, variance, and region-by-region comparability.

Use case summary:
- Internal employee copilot: chat-based Q&A over policy/procedure docs + summarization of customer case notes.
- Embeddings pipeline for doc-search + reranking. Some workloads can tolerate higher latency; the chat assistant has strict p95 expectations.

Workload & performance requirements (from discovery):
- Chat: p95 < 1.5s at peak for typical requests (they described “short prompts, medium answers”). Needs streaming.
- Embeddings: batch-friendly; wants predictable throughput + cost controls.
- They care about “latency/$” as a proxy for unit economics under SLO, but will challenge assumptions (caching/batching/sequence length distribution).

Region / residency requirements:
- Must keep prompt/content processing in EU for regulated business units. Quote from DPO: “We cannot have prompt data routed to US regions, even transiently.”
- Interested in using our EU regions (primary) and only enabling cross-region fallback if they can explicitly opt-in + scope it to non-sensitive traffic.
- Wants clarity on telemetry: what is retained, for how long, and whether any traces can contain customer content.

Product interest:
- Primary: Dedicated in EU for predictable capacity + isolation.
- Secondary: Private (VPC) if their vendor risk process flags shared control plane concerns; asked about timeline + operational model.
- Optimize is interesting if it can provide cost/latency levers with guardrails (they’re currently over-provisioning GPUs internally).

Security/compliance notes:
- Requires SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, retention controls; SOC2/ISO documentation requested.
- They asked for a written statement on: (1) data residency, (2) log redaction/content capture policy, (3) support access controls.

Benchmark report plan (how they will use it):
- Will attach the report to their evaluation doc to justify vendor shortlist + region selection.
- Wants the methodology appendix and “public benchmarking claims” disclaimer language, plus a short FAQ that procurement can understand.
- Asked specifically for: confidence/variance language, rerun policy, and how we avoid cherry-picking models/regions.

What we’ve shared / to share next:
- Queue up: benchmark report landing page + PDF (when public), plus internal-approved Security & Data Handling FAQ stub.
- Include links/stubs:
  - Confluence: sales-enablement/security-faq/benchmark-report-security-and-data-handling-faq.json
  - Confluence: architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/public-benchmarking-claims-guidelines.json
  - Confluence: applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/latency-per-dollar-benchmark-methodology.json

Open questions from the account:
- Can Dedicated guarantee EU-only serving with explicit routing policy + no automatic failover to non-EU regions?
- For Private (VPC): what components are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed? (They asked about control plane location.)
- Can we provide a ‘reproduce a subset’ harness for their workload without exposing sensitive data?

Internal guidance:
- Keep messaging conservative; stick to methodology + constraints (avoid absolute superiority claims). They are sensitive to over-claiming and will escalate to vendor risk if wording is sloppy.
- Bring Markus (SE) to next call to walk through region selection headers/options and fallback behavior; align with Mina Haddad/Ravi Menon if routing policy questions get deep.

Next meeting goal:
- 60-min evaluation session: map their 3 top workloads to a benchmark-aligned config; propose Dedicated EU sizing; outline Private (VPC) alternative path + timelines; agree on what goes into their procurement packet.
